Both denote the Statement's Actor (Agent or Group).
Both denote the xAPI Agent identified by an inverse functional identifier.
Both denote the xAPI Group of Agents, identified or anonymous.
Both denote the xAPI Account (homePage + name) identity structure.
Both denote the contextActivities structure of a Statement's Context.
Both denote the Statement Result (score, success, completion, response, duration).

Both denote the StatementRef object that points to another Statement by id.
Both denote the embedded SubStatement object.
Both denote an IRI-keyed extension; the ontology also types its three placements.
A context extension is the placement of an extension in Statement Context.
A result extension is the placement of an extension in Statement Result.
An activity extension is the placement of an extension in an Activity Definition.
Both denote xAPI's name/document storage; the ontology class generalizes the three document resources.
Interaction activities are described with interaction components (choices, source/target, scale).

Both denote the xAPI Profile defined by the xAPI Profiles specification.
Both denote a Profile's Statement Template.
Both denote a Profile Pattern over Statement Templates.
Both denote a JSONPath-located rule inside a Statement Template.
Both name the organizational record integrating a learner's data across experiences.
A verifiable LER is a checkable form of the record the ELR integrates.
Both name a defined capability that can be assessed and referenced across systems.
The LER class is the definition record of a competency, not the capability itself.
An SCD is a machine-readable competency definition (IEEE 1484.20.3).
Both name an issued, verifiable claim about achievement or qualification.
A micro-credential is a credential scoped to a smaller unit of learning.
An MPL is a specific benchmark level on a proficiency scale.
AI CFT is one competency framework.
The TLA learner profile holds the learner characteristics a learner model represents.
A transactional LRS is a TLA-specific kind of LRS.
An authoritative LRS is a TLA-specific kind of LRS.
A noisy LRS is a TLA-specific kind of LRS.
TLA activity metadata is learning metadata about activities specifically.
Both name an educational or occupational credential that can be issued and recognized.
Both name an organization whose principal purpose is instruction.
A MOOC is a course designed for open access at scale.
OER are learning resources under open licences.
Both name resources used to support teaching and learning.
A VC is one technical form a digital credential can take.
Verifiable LERs are typically expressed as or wrapped in VCs.
A design-time technology affordance is what a runtime hypermedia affordance enacts.

Both mean the management of educational establishments; I2IDL lists the activities involved.
Both concern administering part or the whole of an education system.
Same label and cited as the direct source; I2IDL enumerates the kinds of institution.
Same label and cited as the direct source; I2IDL's definition reuses UNESCO's alternative labels (academic, school facilities).
Same label and cited as the direct source; I2IDL lists what is evaluated.
UNESCO scopes the term to official statements of goals; I2IDL adds principles and directions that shape decisions.

I2IDL's concept adds levels and stages, so UNESCO's Educational systems is narrower.
Teaching methods are one part of what I2IDL's Teaching and training covers.
Training is one part of what I2IDL's Teaching and training covers.
Fields of study versus a kind of formal education: associated, but neither contains the other.
Both denote the xAPI Statement (IEEE 9274.1.1-2023 §5.2.2): Actor, Verb and Object, with an optional Result, Context, timestamp and Attachments.
Both denote the xAPI Verb (§5.2.2.2): an IRI naming the action, with a language map for its display.
Both denote the xAPI Activity (§5.2.2.3): what an Actor interacts with, identified by an IRI.
Both denote the optional Activity Definition metadata object (§5.2.2.3).
Both denote whom a Statement is about (§5.2.2.1): the individual or group performing its action, an Agent or a Group.
I2IDL's concept is the xAPI representation of an individual Actor; the class is the person or system it represents, by the same Inverse Functional Identifier (§5.2.2.1).
I2IDL's concept is the xAPI representation of a collection of Agents; the class is the group it represents, identified or anonymous (§5.2.2.1).
Both denote the xAPI Account (§5.2.2.1): a system's home page and the name of the account on it.
Both denote the contextActivities of a Statement's Context (§5.2.2.5): parent, grouping, category and other.
Both denote the Statement Result (§5.2.2.4): score, success, completion, response, duration and extensions.
Both denote one attachment (§5.2.2.6): an artifact logically part of a Statement, described by usage type, display, content type, length and SHA-2 hash.
Both denote the StatementRef object (§5.2.2.3) that points to another Statement by its id.
Both denote the SubStatement (§5.2.2.3): a Statement nested as the Object of another.
Interaction activities are described with interaction components (choices, scale points, sources and targets, steps).
An xAPI Statement is one machine-readable form of a learning record.
Both denote a Statement's optional Context (§5.2.2.5): registration, context activities, context agents and groups, platform, language, a related Statement, extensions.
Both denote xAPI 2.0's Context Agent (§5.2.2.5): a relationship of one Statement to one Agent, with optional relevant types.
Both denote xAPI 2.0's Context Group (§5.2.2.5): a relationship of one Statement to one Group, with optional relevant types.
I2IDL's concept is the representation of a Group that carries its own Inverse Functional Identifier; the class is the group itself, of either kind (§5.2.2.1).
I2IDL's concept is the representation of a Group known only by its members; the class is the group itself, of either kind (§5.2.2.1).
I2IDL defines it as an Activity Definition with an interaction type (§5.2.2.3) but files it under Activity; related until that is settled.
An extension is one IRI-keyed entry of an extensions map; the class is the map, a node whose properties are the extension IRIs.
xAPI defines its interaction types after SCORM 2004's run-time interactions (cmi.interactions), whose recorded responses the class models.
SCORM's run-time data for one learner's attempt on a SCO is one machine-readable form of a learning record.
A content package's metadata element describes the package or one of its parts: learning metadata in one placement.
An assignable unit is the launchable unit of content a cmi5 course tracks: one kind of digital learning material.
